articles.title: Malaysia to charge two top military officers over alleged corruption
articles.summary: Malaysia's Anti-Corruption Commission announced on Wednesday that it will charge two senior military officers. This action follows a probe into significant allegations of money laundering and graft within the armed forces. The development signals Malaysia's firm stance against corruption, even targeting high-ranking individuals within its defence establishment to ensure integrity.

articles.title: Almost half of Kyiv without heat, power, after Russian attack
articles.summary: An overnight Russian bombardment on Kyiv, Ukraine, on Tuesday, January 20, 2026, caused widespread infrastructure damage. Thousands of residential buildings were left without essential heating and water services amidst extreme -14C temperatures. This attack highlights the ongoing humanitarian crisis and challenges faced by civilians due to the ongoing conflict, demonstrating the impact of military actions on urban infrastructure and population.

articles.title: Mindef reaffirms commitment to transparency and accountability
articles.summary: Malaysia's Defence Ministry (Mindef) has reaffirmed its strong commitment to transparency, accountability, and integrity. This pledge followed a courtesy call from the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief, underscoring ongoing efforts to combat corruption and uphold high ethical standards within defence operations. Such initiatives are crucial for strengthening national security and public confidence in the armed forces.
